Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Quentin wants to borrow the library's portable document scanner for a small batch of old family papers, and the library desk has asked him to send a message before they set the loan aside. He is hoping to pick it up at the Maple Street branch on Thursday around 3 p.m. and bring it back by Friday before closing. those are his preferred times, not something already confirmed. The email should ask whether the scanner is available for that period and whether the branch needs anything from him when he collects it. Keep it friendly and straightforward, and don't make it sound like the loan has been approved or that anyone promised the scanner. Mention that he can be reached by email, but don't invent an address. Please address the message to Quentin, not Mina, and make the draft usable without adding policy details, fees, or equipment instructions that aren't in these notes. It should be concise, but include the pickup and return timing and the questions about availability and collection. The point is only to check the dates and the handoff, not to make a formal complaint or ask for a different device.", "output": "Write a concise, friendly email addressed to Quentin, not Mina, about the library scanner loan. Quentin wants to borrow the library’s portable document scanner for a small batch of old family papers. The library desk has asked him to send a message before setting the loan aside.

Include his preferred schedule: pickup at the Maple Street branch on Thursday around 3 p.m. and return by Friday before closing. Make clear that these times are not confirmed. Ask whether the scanner is available for that period and whether Quentin needs anything when he collects it. Mention that he can be reached by email, but do not make up an address.

Keep the message straightforward and focused on checking availability and the pickup and return arrangements. Do not imply that the loan has been approved or promised, and do not add library policies, fees, equipment instructions, or a request for a different device."}]
